records.raw_text: Minutes of meeting held on 10-12-2015 to discuss about recent chock bearing failures of Bar mill Stands in LMMM
Sri K.V.Vidyasagar, GM(MillS)-Bar       8. Sri SK Nayak, AGM(Oprn)
Sri RLC Patnaik,DGM(Mech)-I/c9. Sri SK Dadel, AGM (Mech)
Sri G V V Satyanarayana,  DGM (Mech)                     10. Sri B.Balaji,AGM(Mech)/RS&RS
Sri P.A. Narasa Raju, DGM(Mech)/RS&RS11. Sri G Chandra Sekhara rao, Sr.Mgr (Mech)
Sri B.Jay Kumar, DGM (Mech)/ RS&RS12. Sri NVR Murthy, Sr.Manager (Oprn)
Sri Ch Sharma, AGM (Mech) 13. Sri D. Murali Mohan, Manager(Mech)
Sri Sriram, AGM (Mech)14. Sri J. Raju, DM(Mech) )/RS&RS
GM(MillS)-Bar  chaired the meeting to discuss about recent chock bearing failures of Bar mill stands  and further actions to be taken up to avoid these failures.
GM(MillS)-Bar addressed all the members and expressed serious concern on frequent  seizures/failures of chock bearings of stands in bar mill and details are given below.

Mr. P.A. Narasa Raju, DGM(Mech) of RS&RS  Dept. informed that roll necks also got damaged for the stands of #22/1, #10 and #12 in addition to failure of bearings in the above cases. Mr. Balaji , AGM(Mech) revealed that in addition to above mentioned, one of the chock bearing from the stand 22/2 came out from line is about to seize /fail.

Regarding above failures, Mr. G. Chandra Sekhara Rao, Sr. Manager(Mech) explained that functioning of doze feeders of the respective stands was checked after failure incident to confirm grease passage to chocks and grease flow was checked by disconnecting the corresponding chock grease hose in the presence of concerned of RS&RS Dept.  In all these failure cases, grease flow to chocks was confirmed.

Mr. G V V Satyanarayana, DGM (Mech)/LMMM informed that the bar mill grease systems 6 caters to Roughing & intermediate train of line 1 and grease system 6.1 caters to intermediate train of line 2 and finishing train. Healthiness of both the grease systems checked and found there is no problem.

a). The existing practices of manual greasing of stand #5 to 8 on Shut down day are being followed. Mid week greasing of stands 20 and 22 of both lines is also being continued for rolling campaign of 16 Re and 20 Re.

b) Recording of roll chock temperatures for the entire bar mill stands is being monitored once in a shift regularly. Now the frequency is to be increased to twice in a shift for some time.                Resp: Mr.G Chandra Sekhara Rao, Sr.Mgr(Mech).

From RS& RS dept, Mr. P.A. Narasa Raju, DGM(Mech) explained the existing assembly practices at RS&Rs dept, and intimated that the probable chances of water ingress in to chocks due to the worn out of sealing ring and mounting area of the roll. He also informed that the stock of the chock bearings is at alarming stage after the replacements for all these failure cases.

GM(MillS)-Bar  advised RS&RS Dept to review the prevailing assembly and mounting practices of bearings and replace the labyrinth seals according to the condition and periodical replacement as part of preventive measure.                                                        Resp: P.A. Narasa Raju, DGM(Mech)

Mr. Murali Mohan, Manager(Mech) revealed that functioning of doze feeders is being checked on shut down day as the maintenance practice for all the stands and record is being maintained in this aspect.

GM(MillS)-Bar  advised to increase the frequency of checking of functioning of doze feeders during pass change times and mill inspection times, which will be implemented immediately.                                     Resp : Mr. Murali Mohan,Mgr(M)

Mr. B.Jay Kumar, DGM (Mech) of RS&RS Det, informed about his visit of bar mill grease systems for monitoring the functioning of system pressures and expressed satisfaction on proper functioning of the grease systems.

Mr. Ch. Sharma, AGM(Mech) explained about the functioning of labyrinth seals and informed about his visit to RS&RS Dept to analyze the assembly and mounting practices. He also informed about failure of bottom chock drive side of BV5 in BDM on 19.11.2015

RS&RS dept. informed that all the stands coming out from the campaign shall be sent to RS&RS dept. for checking the condition of bearing and its parts. Now the existing practice is that the stands coming out from one campaign, which are having pass life are being used in another campaign to fully utilize pass life.  For such stands, the manual greasing of chocks prevails in Bar mill.

Mr. NVR Murthy, Sr.Manager(Opn)/LMMM explained the difficulties in removal and assembly of rolls in the issue of sending spare rolls to RS&Rs Dept. However, keeping in view of condition checking of roll bearings, it is decided to send spare rolls after finishing of rolling campaign to RS&RS dept. from now on wards.                                Resp: Mr. NVR Murthy, Sr.Mgr(Oprn)/LMMM.

GM(MillS)-Bar  informed all the mechanical executives to follow all the existing maintenance practices without fail as per schedules and ensure record keeping of all the prevailing maintenance practices and emphasized about following condition monitoring practices to avoid further failures.         Resp: Mr. GVV Satya Narayana, DGM(M)/LMMM.

GM(MillS)-Bar  concluded the meeting that it is essential to monitor the review of the existing assembly and mounting practices of Bearings and periodical replacement of worn-out parts at RS&RS Dept. and accentuated the increasing the frequency of inspections from LMMM Dept to avoid such failures further.
Minutes of meeting held on 09-02-2016 to discuss about recent chock bearing failures of Bar mill Stands in LMMM
In the month of January, it is observed that two inner races were cracked in Intermediate rolls and one bearing was damaged in finishing rolls. Analysis is going on.
On 8th Feb 2016, Grease system 6.1 was kept in continuous mode and it was observed that it takes around 3.5 hours for full greasing of all finishing chocks.
As per Roll Shop, all roll chocks sent from mill after the campaign had proper grease film.

All rolls should be sent to Roll Shop. Except roughing rolls, no rolls should be reused without the consent of Roll Shop.
All roll chock failures have occurred just last day of the campaign or its previous day.
Lot of water is observed from the Stand 17 chocks while doing manual greasing on 12/01/2016.
Grease samples ( fresh and used ) were collected and sent to FAG & IOCL for detailed analysis.
The advise of the supplier of the Seals (NAK) is also being taken for further sealing improvement.
IOCL personnel also visited the site for studying the failure and further analysis.
Possibilities will be explored to pump excess grease online.

WHILE TRYING TO CHANGE THE RUNNING BLOWER FROM EMERGENCY TO NORMAL, THE MOTOR STARTED TRIPPING ON OVERLOAD AND CAUSING FUSES TO BURN. IT WAS OBSERVED THAT  THE SHAFT MOVEMENT WAS NOT SO FREE i.e. UNABLED  TO BE MOVED BY HAND  ALTHOUGH IT WAS ROTATING BY ROTING THE FAN AFTER OPENING INSPECTION COVER.
ON OPENING THE TOP PART OF PLUMMER BLOCK THE BEARING OUTER RACE OF FAN SIDE WAS FOUND TO BE SKEW. WE COULD NOT SET IT RIGHT IN ITS PLACE AS IT SLIPPED FROM ITS POSITION WHEN ROTATED.

THE FAN COVER WAS REMOVED AND FAN WAS LIFTED AND PLACED AT A HEIGHT BY MEANS OF CHAIN PULLEY. BOTH BEARINGS AND PLUMMER BLOCKS WERE REMOVED. THE BEARINGS WERE REMOVED BY OPENING THE LOCK NUT AND SLIGHTLY HAMMERING THE ADAPTOR SLEEVE. THE FAN SIDE PLUMMER BLOCK’S BOTTOM SURFACE WAS HEAVILY WORN OUT AND IT APPEARED THAT OUTER RACE HAD ROTATED AND CAUSED THE WEAR. THE WEAR OUT WAS CAUSING THE OUTER RACE TO SLIP FROM ITS PLACE.

BOTH PLUMMER BLOCKS WERE REPLACED WITH NEW SKF PLUMMER BLOCK ( SN 513). NEW BEARINGS ( FAG 22213 EK W33) AND NEW ADAPTOR SLEEVES ( H 313 )WERE MOUNTED ON THE SHAFT  AS PER THE DISTANCE BETWEEN BEARING CENTRE GIVEN IN THE DRAWING.

AFTER PLACING THE SHAFT ON THE PLUMMER BLOCK THE BEARING SKEW ( DISTANCE OF OUTER RACE ALONG ITS CIRCUMFERENCE FROM A FIXED POINT ON SHAFT) WAS MEASURED BY MEANS OF DIAL GAUGE. THE SKEW WAS CHECKED AND CORRECTED ONE BY ONE AT BOTH ENDS BY SLIGHTLY LOOSENING THE PLUMMER BLOCK BASE BOLTS AND HAMMERING IN REQUIRED DIRECTION. IT WAS REDUCED FROM 1 mm TO 0.04mm ON FAN SIDE AND FROM .9mm TO .06mm ON MOTOR SIDE.
THE BEARING INTERNAL CLEARANCE WAS CHECKED AND LOCK NUT WAS ACCORDINGLY TIGHTENED. THE STAR WASHER WAS THEN LOCKED. THE INTERNAL CLEARANCE IN BOTH BEARING WAS 0.03mm
ON THE PLUMMER BLOCK ON MOTOR SIDE THE BEARING WAS TO BE LOCATED IN ITS PLACE BY MEANS OF SPACERS ON EITHER SIDE. BUT IT WAS FOUND THAT THERE WAS STILL SOME GAP BETWEEN SPACER AND P.B. HOUSING.
IN ORDER TO FILL IT A ROUND SHIM WAS CUT AND PLACED BETWEEN SPACER AND PLUMMER BLOCK HOUSING. NOW BEARING WAS FIRMLY FIXED.
THE PLUMMER BLOCK WAS FILLED WITH GREASE  AND TIGHTENED. MOTOR ALIGNMENT WAS DONE. THE VIBRATION REDINGS WERE NORMAL.

Role of Looper table in Rolling Mills
In a rolling mill, with individual drives for rolling stands there is
always Tension and Compression in the rolled material. The tension in the
material if not relieved results in distorted/ out of dimension product. To
relieve the tension in the rolled material Loopers are provided between the
stands to form a loop. This Loop is read by a tension control mechanism
relieves the Tension / Compression in the material.
Loopers are very essential for rolling Quality product.
Cost benefit Analysis of the Project:
1) Estimated cost of Looper table from outside procurement           : Rs.
( based on Looper purchased at a cost of Rs.18 Lakhs in Yr 1996)
2) The Cost of all internal resources used
Bar rolling is the most dynamic and challenging in hot rolling process. It is due to real time changes in dimensional tolerance .
Looper  plays a predominant role in bar rolling .
In bar rolling the stock moves from one stand to another stand till the finishing stands where it gets required size and shape.

When the stock moves from the one stand to other stand the tension is increased or decreased in the stock due to speed variation in the motors of the stands due to change in tension in the bar the dimensional quality of the bar affected and uneven increase or decrease in width wise of stock may happen.
In order to avoid the tension between the stand, loopers are incorporated . Loopers ensure tension free rolling in between the stands by providing loop.
In VSP, loopers are employed in bar mill and wire & rod mill.
Loopers are either vertical or horizontal. Horizontal loopers are for bar rolling and vertical loopers are for flat cross sections. The present discussion is an horizontal looper of bar mill.

Between each stand of the finishing mill, a looper is provided which serves to deflect and guide the bar to form a loop for tension free rolling. Loop formation depends on the speed difference between two stands. The loop length being controlled by a meaning lead.
1. Looping table which is shiftable by hydraulic cylinder.

The rolling stock is moved across the looper by means of guides and introduced in to next stand. The tip of rolling stock touches the rolls of the next stand ,loop formation starts and looper is in operation till the stock moves from the stand.
2. Provision for speed variation between stands to  know the dimensional accuracy
3. Fin controlling due to loop formation.
4. Uniform dimension through out the bar.
5. Uniform  properties due to dimensional accuracy.
6. Controlling the tension in the bar.
Cobble may take place inside the looper during loop formation when there is an abnormal speed variation in the stands speed.
To avoid cobbles in the  looper now a days , new technologies are coming to eliminate loopers in rooling till these systems are not time tested in hot rooling mills.
A team from Bar mill of LMMM ……………………………. Made a Horizontal Looper and fabricated a looper  with inhouse resources and put in line which is running successfully.
They saved Rs.40,00,000 to the company by way of fabricating it with inhouse resources and producing a qualitative looper.
Their efforts are well appreciated by GM(W)I/C and other senior officials of VSP.

THE INPUT AND BOTTOM END COVERS OF GEARBOX WERE THEN OPENED FOR INSPECTION. OIL FLOW WAS FOUND SATISFACTORY AND VISIBLE BEARINGS WERE SEEN TO BE NORMAL. HOWEVER, A SMALL CHUNK OF BEARING ROLLER WAS RETRIEVED FROM THE TOP INSPECTION COVER OPENING. THE TEMPERATURE AT ECR SIDE TOP WAS BETWEEN 64-65 COMAPRED TO AROUND 50 FOR OTHER BEARINGS.
IT WAS DECIDED TO CHANGE THE STAND HOUSING. AFTER REPLACEMENT OF STAND HOUSING ON NEXT DAY, THE ABNORMAL HUMMING SOUND REDUCED BY 90 %, ALMOST GONE.

THE TEMPERATURE REMAINED HIGHER ON ECR SIDE TOP AREA – AROUND 64. VIBRATIONS WERE IN RANGE. IN VIEW OF THE FINDING OF BEARING ROLLER PIECE AND HIGH TEMP, IT WAS DECIDED TO GO FOR THE GEARBOX REPLACEMENT IN COMING SHUTDOWN ON 08-03-2022 WHEN 16R SECTION WAS TO BE ROLLED.
THE SPARE EISENBISS GEARBOX WAS INSTALLED IN LINE. FOLLOWING ARE THE DETAILS AVAILABLE REGARDING THE REVISIONING ACTIVITY AT CMS.

CAME OUT FROM STAND 21/1 ON 03-06-2018. LONG O/P SHAFT TOP BEARING FAILED DUE TO OIL SCARCITY.RETURNED TO LMMM ON 27/02/2019. CHECKED OIL FLOW ON 23-04-2019, LONG O/P TOP BEARING POINT WAS JAMMED. IT WAS CLEARED BY HYD. OIL FLOW OK NOW.READY TO USE. SENT TO CMS ON 31-08-2021 FOR CHANGING LONG SHAFT BOTTOM BEARING FROM NTN NON MATCHED TO MATCHED FAG BEARING. 30230X/DF FAG BEARING INSTALLED.RECEIVED ON 14-09-2021. OIL FLOW CHECKED.OK

SENT TO CMS ON 08/12/2018. ON DISMANTLING, IT WAS FOUND THAT BOTTOM BEVEL GEAR TOOTHS WERE DAMAGED IN 7 TO 8 PLACES DUE TO FALLING OF ROLLERS. ONE INPUT SHAFT(THAT CAME OUT WHEN THE OTHER SPARE HOUSING  WAS USED FOR MAKING STAND 16 GEARBOX AT CMS) AND ONE NEW BEVEL GEAR WAS SENT TO CMS IN DEC18THE INPUT SHAFT AFTER REMOVING THE BEVEL GEAR AND THE DAMAGED BEVEL GEAR AND ITS PAIR(FROM THE 21/1 GEARBOX THAT WAS SENT) WAS RETURNED TO STORES ON 14/02/2019.THE GEARBOX WAS SHIFTED TO LMMM ON 27/02/2019. THE INPUT AND MATCHING BEVEL GEAR PAIR WAS REPLACED. ALL BEARINGS WERE REPLACED. NO OTHER PARTS WERE REPLACED AS PER THE INFO AVAILABLE
BOTH LIFT TABLE GEARBOXES WERE REPLACED WITH REVISIONED ONES.
BOTH BELLOWS AND ITS SEATING PIPES WERE REPLACED.
HOOD AND PROTECTION SHELLS WERE REPLACED WITH NEW ONES

IT WAS DECIDED TO CHANGE THE SHAFTS, BUT THE REVISIONED SHAFTS DID NOT ENTER THE HUB. AFTER LOT OF TRYING, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE SHELL WAS OFFSET AND PREVENTING THE MATCHING OF STUDS AND HOLES. THE SHELL WAS OPENED AND GEARBOX LOWERED AND THEN TRIED AGAIN WITHOUT SUCCESS.

THE PCD WAS NOT MATCHING. ALL STUDS WERE NOT ENTERING IN FLANGE HOLES AND FLANGE WAS GETTING TAPERED. IT WAS DECIDED TO PUT OLD SHAFTS IN LINE. THE WRM SIDE SHAFT ENTERED IN PLACE AFTER HAMMERING. THE ECR SIDE SHAFT FLANGE HOLES WERE ENLARGED AND THEN FIXED ON THE OUTPUT HUB. THE GEARBOX WAS THEN LIFTED AND SHELL BOLTS TIGHTENED ON THE HOOD.
BECAUSE OF THE SHAFT PROBLEM THE JOB WAS COMPLTED BY 01:20 AM ON 10-03-2022 i.e. FROM 08-03-2022 06:00 HRS TO  10-03-2022 01:20 HRS.
THE GEARBOX IS RUNNING FINE. FOLLOWING ARE THE VIBRATION READINGS

The Stand 16 main gearbox was installed in line in CR-2018 (refer history). On 17-08-2021, Stand 16 drive got stopped on account of lub oil fault at around 11 A.M. When checked, the gauge reading was 1.2 bar. When the gauge pressure was increased to 2 bar, oil started to come out of the long output shaft bottom bearing end cover by overflowing. The temperature was found normal. When the end cover was opened, it was found that the long output bottom bearing was damaged.
The gearbox replacement job started at 11:30A.M.The completion of job and handing over to Operations was at 20:00 hrs on 18-08-2021.

IT WAS DECIDED TO PLACE SHIMS OF DIFFERENT THICKNESS FOR BOTH ROWS OF THE SPHERICAL ROLLER BEARING 24052. THE WIDTH WAS ABOUT THE FLAT SURFACE OF OUTER RACE OF ONE ROW OF BEARING.
INITIALLY BEARING RETAINER WAS USED ON HOUSING SURFACE AS SEEN IN THE ABOVE PHOTOGRAPHS. BUT IT WAS REMOVED BEFORE FINAL ASSEMBLING AS IT WAS FORMING A VERY HARD UNEVEN SURFACE.

Smoke was observed from the top knife shaft middle bearing at start of A shift.  The bearing end cover was opened and bearing was found to be damaged and totally dry indicating no oil flow to the bearing. The nozzle was found to be jammed.
The dismantling started at 08:00 A.M. The shaft, after cutting of all 3 bearings at workshop, was sent to CMS at 01:30 P.M. and received at 08:30 P.M. Rolling started at 2 A.M.
All 3 bearings of top knife shaft were replaced.
The seal in the end cover of damaged bearing was replaced.
The spacer ring next to middle bearing (one that failed) had become oval. The ring was cut in 2 halves, made as round as possible, and installed.
The double porter bar was removed and applied after fixing round plates at the ends of bearing to avoid skewness.( The plates were taken from slings cupboard by side of CP-5).
While fixing, the DP Bar was heated to about 120 degrees. The Bar was fixed in position by
The hydraulic nuts were tightened by means of tensioner at 350Bar.
Extra oil lines and nozzles were provided at the top and bottom shaft middle bearing and oil flow was thoroughly checked for all the bearings

Abnormal sound was observed last day from shear 14.1 during its operation. It was found that input shaft (towards fin area) bearing 23230 CC/W33 on ECR side was completely damaged. There was no oil and rollers had come out.
By 6.00 a.m. on 11/07/2014 D.P. bar, top part, and middle part of housing was opened. Studs were opened by hydraulic tensioner (HT-1) at 500 bar.
Round metal plates were used to aid the removal of D.P. bar (to keep 23230 brg outer race in its position). plates were taken from slings cupboard.
The bearing cover was opened and input shaft was removed.

The damage of bearing had caused scarring of the shaft at inner race area .While mounting the bearing, it stopped before its position. The bearing was removed and the shaft surface was carefully prepared and another bearing was mounted.
Assembling started from 5.00 p.m. and was fully assembled and ready by 5.00 a.m. next day. The D.P. bar did not require any heating while assembling and hammering was enough.
** While assembling, the clutch was in neutral position and its jaws were not in coupled condition.

After assembling it was found that the clutch position could not be put into coupled mode by its lever handle as the gear wheel was not free on the shaft. In order to make it free the input shaft towards fin area was locked by locking the  knives while the input shaft towards BDM was rotated at its coupling by means of chain pulley. The gear became free and the clutch was put into coupled mode.
The shear was handed over to Operations at starting of A shift.
